    Kaveri River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES         Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Puducherry

         ORIGIN          Brahmagiri Hills at Talakaveri in Kodagu (Coorg) District (Karnataka)

                            Tamil Nadu – River enters through Dharmapuri District and drops into
                         Hogenakkal Falls

                            Kaveri enters Puducherry through Karaikal as the Noolar river

        TERMINATES    South of Cuddalore (Tamil Nadu) into Bay of Bengal

                          Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkaveri, Chovrai, Turunananimuttai, Lakshmantirath,
         TRIBUTARIES
                              Kabini, Bhavani, Noyil, Amravati, Kollidam, Thenpennaiyar

                          Bhavani is the major tributary.

                            Tamil Nadu - Amaravathi Dam, Upper Anaicut (Mukkombu), Mettur Dam,
       DAMS
                              Kallanai Dam

                          Karnataka - Krishnaraja Sagara Dam, Mekedatu Dam project (proposed)

                            Kerala - Banasura Sagar Dam on Kabini River

         HILLS           Brahmagiri Hill, Kodagu Hills, Nilgiri Hills

        FACTS         The river is the third largest in South India after Godavari and Krishna,
                        and it is the largest river in Tamil Nadu. In Mandya District (Karnataka), it

                         Shivanasamudra Falls.

    Krishna River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES         Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh

         ORIGIN         Mahabaleshwar (Maharashtra)

                       The river enters Karnataka at Kurundwad

                        Tungbhadra river meets Krishna River near Alampur village in
                       Mehaboobnagar District of Telangana

                         Andhra?

                       The river merges into the Bay of Bengal at Hamasaladeevi (Andhra
        TERMINATES
                          Pradesh)

                        Tungabhadra (largest), Mallaprabha, Koyna, Bhima, Ghataprabha, Yerla,
         TRIBUTARIES
                         Warna, Dindi, Musi and Dudhganga

       DAMS          Telangana - Nagarjuna Sagar Dam, Koilsagar Dam (on which tributary)

                        Andhra Pradesh - Srisailam Dam

                          Karnataka - Tungabhadra Dam (Pampa Sagar), Basava Sagara (Formerly
                      known as Narayanpura Dam), Mallaprabha Dam

                          Maharashtra - Ujjani Dam, Koyna Dam

         HILLS          Bhimashankar hills (Maharashtra)

        FACTS          Also known as Krishnaveni

                            Fourth-biggest river in terms of water inflows and river basin area after the
                         Ganga, Godavari and Brahmaputra

                          Nagarjuna Sagar Dam— one of the world's largest and tallest Masonry dam

                          Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh) is the largest city on the River Krishna

                           Pritisangam is a place where Krishna river and Koyna river meet each other.

                        Koyna Dam is the largest dams in Maharashtra, constructed on Koyna river
                        and Hydroelectric Project is the largest completed hydroelectric power
                              plant in India.

    Godavari River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

                           Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh,
        STATES
                           Odisha, Karnataka and Puducherry





Indian Rivers and Dams                                                                                                              2

CATEGORY     DETAILS

         ORIGIN         Source is in Triambakeshwar, Nasik, Maharashtra

                          Empties via its two mouths: the Gautami Godavari to the north and the Vasishta
        TERMINATES
                          Godavari to the south.

                       The Gautami branch splits into two branches — Gautami and Nilarevu

                       The Vasishta splits into two branches — Vasishta and Vainateya

                        These four branches join the Bay of Bengal at different places

                            Pravara, Purna, Manjira, Manair, Pranhita (largest), Indravati, Sabari, Wainganga,
         TRIBUTARIES
                           Bindusara

       DAMS          Maharashtra - Gangapur Bandh Sagar, Jayakwadi Dam, Ghatghar Dam

                          Telangana - Sriram Sagar Dam (Pochampadu Project)

                        Andhra Pradesh - Polavaram Project (Under construction)

         HILLS           Satmala hills, Mahadeo hills, Papi Hills, Ajanta Range

        FACTS         Second largest river after Ganga

                           Also known as Dakshina Ganga – Ganges of the South

                          Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India

                         Paderu is the highest peak in the Godavari river basin as well as in Eastern
                            Ghats.

    Narmada River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES        Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat

         ORIGIN          Rises from Amarkantak Plateau (Narmada Kund) near Anuppur district (MP)

        TERMINATES    Drains from Gulf of Khambhat (Gulf of Cambay) (Gujarat) into the Arabian Sea

                      Tawa River (longest) , Shakkar River, Hiran River, Sher River, Ganjal River, Dudhi
         TRIBUTARIES
                             River

       DAMS           Gujarat - Sardar Sarovar Dam

                      Madhya Pradesh - Maheshwar Dam, Indira Sagar Dam, Goi Dam, Jobat Dam
                           (Shahid Chandra Shekhar Azad Sagar Project), Omkareshwar Dam

         HILLS           Vindhya Range, Maikala Range, Satpura Range

        FACTS          Also known as Rewa.

                     Known as Life Line of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh

                        Runs from East to West (longest west flowing river), along with the Tapti River
                        and the Mahi River

                         Flows between Vindhya Range and Satpura Range





Indian Rivers and Dams                                                                                                              3

CATEGORY     DETAILS

                       The Dhuandhar Falls are located on Narmada River in Bhedaghat (Jabalpur
                                 District – MP)

     Tapti (Tapi) River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES        Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat

         ORIGIN        From Multai in Betul district of Madhya Pradesh

        TERMINATES    Drains from Gulf of Khambhat (Gulf of Cambay) (Gujarat) into the Arabian Sea

         TRIBUTARIES    Mindhola River, Purna River, Gima River, Panjhra River, Vaghur River, Bori River

       DAMS           Gujarat - Ukai Dam (Vallabh Sagar)

                          Maharashtra - Hatnur Dam, Dhaner Dam

         HILLS           Gawilgarh Hills, Satpura Range

        FACTS                 It flows westward – From East to West

    Mahi River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES        Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat

                                              It originates from Vindhyachal Hills in Madhya Pradesh and after flowing through
         ORIGIN
                            the Vagad region of Rajasthan, enters Gujarat

        TERMINATES    Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea) - Gujarat

         TRIBUTARIES   Som River (Principle tributary), Anas River, Panam River

       DAMS           Rajasthan - Banswara Dam or Mahi Bajaj Sagar Dam

                             Gujarat - Wanakbori Dam, Kadana Dam

                                              It is one of the many west-flowing rivers in India along with Tapti River,
        FACTS
                          Sabarmati River, Luni River and Narmada River.

    Mahanandi River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES          Chhattisgarh, Odisha

         ORIGIN          Siwaha, Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh

                       The Seonath River meets Mahanadi at Bilaspur District

                            Enters the Odisha plains at Naraj

        TERMINATES    Just before entering Cuttack, it gives off a large Distributary called the Kathjori.





Indian Rivers and Dams                                                                                                              4

CATEGORY     DETAILS

                       The Mahanadi (Birupa) and Brahmani rivers together form a large delta and
                             drains into Bay of Bengal at Dhamra (Odisha)

                              Also, it enters the Odisha plains near Cuttack and enters the Bay of Bengal at
                          Paradeep, False Point by several channels

                           Shivnath River (Seonath River – Longest Tributary), Tel River, Mand River,
         TRIBUTARIES
                       Hasdeo River, Sondur River, Jonk River

                         Seonath River originates from Rajnandgaon District of Chhattisgarh and meets
                        Mahanadi at Bilaspur District.

       DAMS          Odisha - Hirakud Dam, Manibhadra dam (proposed)

                            Chhattisgarh - Dudhawa Dam, Gangrel Dam (Ravi Shankar Sagar Dam), Sondur
                       Dam, Hasdeo Bango Dam

         HILLS           Satpura Range, Lamdungri Hills on the left and the Chandili Dunguri on the right.

                          Hirakud is one of the first major multipurpose river valley projects started after
        FACTS
                               India's independence.

                         Brahmani River is NOT a tributary of Mahanadi. It’s a seasonal river that flows in
                           Odisha.

    Brahmaputra River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES         Arunachal Pradesh and Assam

                             Originates on the Angsi Glacier located on the northern side of the Himalayas in
         ORIGIN
                         Burang County of Tibet.

                         (The source of the river was earlier thought to be on the Chemayungdung
                               glacier)

                            Enters India through Arunachal Pradesh (Dihang or Siang River)

                            Enters Assam (Brahmaputra River)

        TERMINATES     In Bangladesh (Jamuna River), the Brahmaputra is joined by the Teesta River.

                        Below the Tista, the Brahmaputra splits into two distributary branches.

                       The western branch continues due south as the Jamuna and merges with the
                           lower Ganga called the Padma River.

                       The eastern branch is called the lower or old Brahmaputra joins the Meghna
                             River near Dhaka.

                       The Padma and Meghna converge near Chandpur and flow out into the Bay of
                            Bengal.

                            This final part of the river is called Meghna.

                         Dibang or Sikang River, Lohit River, Dhansiri River, Kolong River, Manas River,
         TRIBUTARIES
                          Teesta River, Beki River, Raidak River, Jaldhaka River, Subansiri River





Indian Rivers and Dams                                                                                                              5

CATEGORY     DETAILS

                                              It is lifeline of Sikkim and makes a border between Sikkim and West Bengal
        TEESTA
                           before joining the Brahmaputra as a tributary in Bangladesh. Largest tributary of
          (TISTA) RIVER
                         Brahmaputra (Originating in Sikkim, India)

       DAMS          Arunachal Pradesh - Dibang Dam

                           Sikkim - Rangit Dam

                          Border of Assam and Arunachal Pradesh - Subansiri Lower Dam

                             Tibet - Pangduo Hydro Power Station

                          China - Zangmu Dam

        FACTS          Also called Tsangpo-Brahmaputra

                                              It is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet.

                        Sundarbans Delta — The Sundarbans is a mangrove area in the delta formed by
                            the confluence of Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna Rivers in the Bay of
                            Bengal.

   Yamuna River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES         Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Delhi

                              Originating from Yamunotri Glacier on the slopes of Banderpooch peaks,
         ORIGIN
                             Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand

                              After passing the Sikh pilgrimage town of Paonta Sahib (Himachal Pradesh), the
                      Yamuna reaches Tajewala in Yamuna Nagar district of Haryana.

                                              It enters Delhi near Palla village, Wazirabad.

                                              It merges with the Ganges at Triveni Sangam, Allahabad which is a site of the
        TERMINATES
                     Kumbh Mela.

                        Tons River (Largest Tributary), Chambal River (Longest Tributary), Sindh River,
         TRIBUTARIES
                       Betwa River, Ken River

                        Tons River originates from Bandarpunch, Uttarakhand and merges with Yamuna
                                 in Dehradun.

                       Chambal River forms boundary between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh before
                             turning southeast to join the Yamuna in Uttar Pradesh.

                         Hindon River

         HILLS            Shiwalik Hills, Doon Valley

       DAMS          Haryana - Hathni Kund Barrage

                          Uttarakhand - Lakhwar-Vyasi Dam Project

                          Uttarakhand-Himachal Pradesh border - Asan Barrage

                      Madhya Pradesh - Gandhi Sagar Dam (Bhadra)





Indian Rivers and Dams                                                                                                              6

CATEGORY     DETAILS

                           Rajasthan - Ranapratap Sagar Dam

                       The Yamuna does not pass across Himachal Pradesh, but receives water from
        FACTS
                               that state via the Tons.

    Ganga River

        CATEGORY     DETAILS

        STATES         Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal

         ORIGIN                 It originates from Gangotri Glacier

                       The main stream of the Ganges begins at the confluence of the Bhagirathi and
                         Alaknanda rivers at Devprayag (Garhwal), Uttarakhand originating from the
                      Chaukhamba range of glaciers

                              After entering West Bengal, divides into two rivers: the Hooghly River and the
                     Padma River

                              After entering Bangladesh near Chapai Nababganj, Padma is joined by the
                      Jamuna River where the two join and form the Meghna River.

                       The Hooghly flows through several districts of West Bengal and falls into the Bay
        TERMINATES
                             of Bengal near Sagar Island.

                       The Padma also flows into and through Bangladesh and also empties into the
                        Bay of Bengal.

                       The Meghna River then branches into a set of distributaries which eventually
                             drain into the Bay of Bengal.

                      Ramganga River, Gomti River, Karnali River, Gandaki River, Koshi River,
         TRIBUTARIES
                       Mahananda River

                      Yamuna River (Longest), Tamsa River, Son River, Rishiganga River, Hanuman
                       Ganga River

                         Hooghly River is the DISTRIBUTARY of Ganga

         HILLS         Chaukhamba Range

       DAMS           Uttarakhand - Tehri Dam, Koteshwar Dam, Maneri Dam

        FACTS         Ganga joins the Yamuna at the Triveni Sangam at Allahabad.

                       The Farakka Barrage was created by India in 1975 to divert water from the
                       Ganges River to the Bhagirathi-Hoogly river system.

                            Five Prayags —

                          Vishnuprayag — Alaknanda and Dhauliganga River (Chamoli district,
                           Uttarakhand)

                        Nandaprayag — Alaknanda and Nandakini River (Chamoli)

                         Karnaprayag — Alaknanda and Pindar River (Chamoli)

                         Rudraprayag — Alaknanda and Mandakini (Rudraprayag)





Indian Rivers and Dams                                                                                                              7

CATEGORY     DETAILS

                        Devprayag — Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meet and take the name Ganga (Tehri
                          Garhwal)

    Indus River

        CATEGORY         DETAILS

        STATES/COUNTRY   India – Jammu and Kashmir

                                  Pakistan, China

         ORIGIN               Originates near the Mansarovar Lake in the Tibetan plateau

                                      In Kashmir, it crosses the Ladakh district and in Baltistan District enters
                                Pakistan Administered Kashmir .

        TERMINATES              It ends in Arabian Sea near Karachi

                                Ravi River, Beas River, Satluj River, Jhelum River , Kishenganga River
         TRIBUTARIES        (Neelum) and Chenab River (Largest), Soan River, Zanskar River, Shyok
                                     River, Hunza River

       DAMS           Jammu and Kashmir - Pakal Dul Dam (Proposed)

                                Pakistan - Bunji Dam/Rondu Bunji Dam/Haramosh Bunji Dam (Proposed)

                                Leh, Ladakh - Dumkhar Dam (proposed dam)

        FACTS            The ‘Indus Valley Civilization’ was born around this river.

                                                     It is Pakistan’s longest river.

                              Punjab means "The Land of Five Waters", referring to the rivers Jhelum,
                             Chenab, Ravi, Sutlej and Beas.

     Sutlej River

        CATEGORY        DETAILS

        STATES/COUNTRY  India – Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan

                             China and Pakistan

         ORIGIN           West of Lake Rakshastal in Tibet

                                                   It enters India in Himachal Pradesh near Shipki La Pass

                                                   It meets the Beas River near Makhu, Firozpur District, Punjab

        TERMINATES            It enters Pakistan about 15 kilometres east of Bhedian Kalan, Punjab

                                                   It unites with the Chenab River forming the Panjnad River, which finally flows
                                    into the Indus river near Bahawalpur, Punjab, Pakistan.

         TRIBUTARIES         Spiti River, Beas River and Baspa River

                             Himachal Pradesh - Bhakra Dam, Koldam Dam Hydropower Project, Nathpa
       DAMS
                                Jhakri Dam





Indian Rivers and Dams                                                                                                              8

CATEGORY        DETAILS

        FACTS              Also known as Satadree

    Chenab River

        CATEGORY        DETAILS

        STATES/COUNTRY  Jammu and Kashmir

                               Pakistan

                          The river is formed from the confluence of the Chandra and the Bhaga
         ORIGIN
                                   rivers on the opposite sides of the Baralacha pass (Himachal Pradesh)

                             Confluence with Sutlej to form the Panjnad River near Bahawalpur District,
        TERMINATES
                               Punjab, Pakistan

         TRIBUTARIES       Marsudar RIver

       DAMS          Jammu and Kashmir - Baglihar Dam, Dul Hasti Dam

        FACTS                Traditionally known as Chandrabhaga River
